hint: Some endings come in two shapes. Look at the vowels of the word they attach to.

corpus.en: The pipers do not milk the goats.

toEnglish.explanation: V S order. moma = dance; num = NEG; nitite-li-se = piper-PL-DEF. One participant, so no ergative ending.

toLang.prompt: A piper does not milk the goat.
toLang.explanation: V S O order. önö = milk; num = NEG; nitite-ti = piper-ERG; ete-se = goat-DEF.

grammar: Word order: verb, subject, object. With one participant: verb, subject.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
Ergative: marks the doer of a two-participant verb. The lone participant of a one-participant verb is bare, just like the object.
Negation: a separate word after the verb.
explain.notes: Vowel harmony: a word's vowels are either all back (a, o, u) or all front (e, ö, i), and suffix vowels follow the stem. Checked against 988 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 976, including: -lu/-li appears when: definite; -lu/-li appears when: plural & definite.
